## TL;DR

I checked the docs site at 375, 768 and 1280 px in headless WebKit and found three real defects, all fixed. Links: 39 of 1,873 internal links were broken; they are fixed, and a link check now gates `bun run build`. Code blocks: on every block the copy button painted over the `bash` language label, so the label was unreadable at every width; the label now sits top-left. Nav and search (sidebar, phone menu, local search) worked at all three widths and needed no change. The QA record is `docs/qa/2026-11-docs-site-nav-qa.md`. The scoped `repoos check --changed main` passed.

## Work and rationale

The task asked for a headless pass over the docs site, a link check, fixes with tests, and the QA record. I built `user-docs/` with `bun run build`, served it with `vitepress preview`, and drove it with Playwright's WebKit. No visible browser was opened.

**Links.** VitePress is configured with `ignoreDeadLinks: [/^\.{1,2}\//]`, so the build never checked relative links. I added `user-docs/scripts/check-links.ts`. It walks every rendered page in `.vitepress/dist` and resolves each internal `href` and `src` the way a browser does on the published site, including `#fragments` against the target page's ids. It runs as the last step of `bun run build`, so the existing `user-docs-build` gate in `repoos.toml` enforces it without touching that file. It found three kinds of breakage. Twenty changelog section links pointed at `#highlights`, but the loader prefixes release headings with the tag, so the target was `#v0-5-92--highlights`. Sixteen links from pages such as `/cli` and `/configuration` pointed at `../docs/…`, which exists on a checkout but 404s on the site. Three anchors had drifted from their headings. I fixed the changelog in the loader (`release-heading-ids.ts`), pointed the `../docs/` links at the same files on GitHub (the form `android-hub.md` already uses), and corrected the three anchors to the ids the build emits. After the fix the check reports 1,857 internal links resolving.

**Code-block labels.** VitePress puts the language label at `top: 2px; right: 8px` and the copy button at `top: 12px; right: 12px`, so they always collide. I first moved the label left of the button, which fixed the button overlap but painted the label over the visible text of the install command. The final rule in `custom.css` puts the label top-left, in the padding above the first code line, with `line-height: 1` so its box does not touch the code. The first version of the overlap gate counted boxes that only touched at a fractional pixel; I tightened the label and kept a strict gate.

**Shared rules.** The page rules (overflow, element past the viewport, label overlap) live in `user-docs/scripts/layout-metrics.ts`. The browser test `layout.test.ts` and the QA sweep `docs/qa/measure-docs-site-widths.mjs` both use them. The test boots its own preview on a free port.

## Approaches tried

- A `bun:test` link checker over fixtures, plus the same check in the build. The build is what the gate actually runs, so the check lives there. The unit tests cover the resolution rules, and the table-driven cases include escaping paths and missing fragments.
- Repo-wide sweep first, then targeted tests. The sweep covers 29 routes at 3 widths (87 page loads, 471 code blocks), which is what found the label overlap. It is in `docs/qa` because it is the QA artifact the task asked for.
- Removing the label rule to prove the test fails. With the rule removed, `layout.test.ts` fails on every page at every width. The rule is restored and rebuilt.

## Challenges and blockers

- **A stale preview looked like a product bug.** I rebuilt the docs while `vitepress preview` was running. The preview kept serving the old hashed entry bundle, which returned 404, so the client app never hydrated and the phone Menu button did nothing. The fix was to restart the preview on the new output. The sweep and tests now run against a fresh preview each time.
- **My own harness was wrong in three places.** The home page has its title in the hero, not `.vp-doc h1`. The CLI page's h1 is "CLI reference", not "CLI". A client-side route change updates the URL before the content, so I had to wait for the h1 text rather than the URL. I also clicked before hydration, and waited on a `.VPNavScreen.active` class that VitePress does not set. Each is fixed, and I noted them so the next pass does not repeat them.
- **The repo's test runner does not cover `user-docs/`.** The root `vitest` run does not pick up `user-docs/scripts`, and `repoos.toml` is off-limits here. So `bun test scripts` in `user-docs/` (53 tests, including the browser layout test) is not part of `repoos check`, the same as the existing `worker.test.ts`. The build gate does cover links. Closing the gap needs a human edit to `repoos.toml`.

## Evidence and what is not verified

- Scoped `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`: all checks passed, with no failed steps. The user-docs build, link check, UI smoke and the scoped test run were green. The step table lists `tests` as skipped for the remote validation runner, but the run executed 784 test cases with none failing. I did not run the full unscoped suite.
- `bun test scripts` in `user-docs/`: 53 pass, including 18 browser tests.
- The QA sweep: no overflow, nav or search failures at 375, 768 and 1280.
- Not verified: external links, including the GitHub `blob/main` targets and the `#…-0761` anchor on `previews.md`, which I could not fetch. Dark and Gruvbox themes at these widths. A 768 px screenshot. Real devices and touch input. Those are listed in the QA record.

## Key learnings

- A relative-link check that VitePress skips is a silent gap. Checking the rendered HTML catches it, and so does a link to a repo file, which needs a GitHub URL on the published site.
- VitePress slugs are not the heading text. A leading digit becomes `_2-…`, an apostrophe becomes `-`, and `repoos story new|list|show|update` becomes `repoos-story-new-list-show-update`. Link to the emitted id, and let the check catch drift.
- A loader that rewrites heading ids must rewrite the header-anchor `href` too, or the permalink points nowhere.
- When a clickable control "does nothing", check the network first. A single 404 on the entry bundle makes the whole app inert, and it looks exactly like a UI bug.
- Two overlays in the same corner collide at every width. Fixing one placement can move the collision onto content. Check the label against code text as well as against the button.
